---
title: "Workspace Setup"
---

Before we start, let's make sure everyone has a working Python environment with the right packages installed.

## Option A — Anaconda (Recommended for NHS Laptops)

1. Download **Anaconda Individual Edition** from [anaconda.com/download](https://www.anaconda.com/download) (free).
2. Install it, accepting the default settings.
3. Open **Anaconda Navigator** → click **Launch** next to **JupyterLab**.
4. In a terminal (or Anaconda Prompt on Windows), install the extra packages:

```bash
conda install -c conda-forge scikit-learn seaborn
```

## Option B — pip

If you have Python 3.9+ already:

```bash
pip install pandas matplotlib seaborn scikit-learn jupyterlab
```

## Option C — Binder (No Installation)

Click the badge below to launch a pre-configured environment in your browser — no installation needed:

[![Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org)

::: {.callout-note}
## Required packages

| Package | Version | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|
| `pandas` | ≥ 2.0 | Data manipulation |
| `matplotlib` | ≥ 3.7 | Plotting |
| `seaborn` | ≥ 0.13 | Statistical visualisation |
| `scikit-learn` | ≥ 1.4 | Machine learning |
| `numpy` | ≥ 1.26 | Numerical operations |
:::

## Download the Course Data

Download `nhs_readmission.csv` from the course repository and place it in your working directory. You can verify everything is set up correctly by running this in a new notebook cell:

```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier

print("All packages loaded successfully!")
df = pd.read_csv("nhs_readmission.csv")
print(f"Dataset loaded: {df.shape[0]} patients, {df.shape[1]} columns")
```

If you see the success messages, you're ready to go!
